**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

```

      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}

      # runs the JS-engine test family pre-merge on macos (the surface the

      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/cli/trajectory_|^bin/fah\.dart$|^test/(integration/)?trajectory/|^flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service(_sessions)?\.dart$)'; then
            echo "perf=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # gh-1241 REG-1: the usage fold consumes the trajectory ledger's
          # model_request_summary records and the session chain's shape —
          # a red usage-fold suite blocks the merge even when the regular
          # legs are green.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/session/|^lib/src/usage/|^test/usage/|^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$)'; then
            echo "usagefold=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion zone. The ubuntu flutter-tests
          # leg runs this family but every engine-dependent test SKIPS there
          # (native_test_guard.dart finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner);
          # the tests truly execute only in the nightly macOS leg — the hole
          # #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an apps/engine regression merged
          # green, went red the same night). The issue's packages/
          # js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its bumps arrive
          # via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
  # only prove the SBPL PROFILE TEXT (unit + guard/profile parity) — the
  # kernel's last-match-wins read/write enforcement of rw mounts under a
  # read-denied prefix needs a real `sandbox-exec` run, which exists only on
  # macOS. Both live suites skip with a NAMED reason wherever they cannot
  # run (no sandbox-exec / already-sandboxed host / HOME outside /Users) —
  # the skip lands in the job log, never silent; this leg is where they
  # actually execute. The leg is a real gate input: `quality-gate` NEEDS it

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

    ...

```

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart

  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night). When
  # a PR touches the exclusion zone (flutter_app/lib/apps/**,
  # lib/src/js_ext/**, the guarded family, the guard itself, or the external
  # js_widget_runtime pin in flutter_app/pubspec.yaml), this macos leg runs
  # the family pre-merge, where JavaScriptCore actually loads. Rare paths →
  # one cheap runner; every other PR pays nothing. Nightly keeps the
  # full-suite macOS backstop; merge-blocking flows through the aggregate
  # Quality gate (a red exzone = red gate, AC1's required-and-green).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.

- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

This workflow has **no `pull_request` trigger** (dispatch-only CI, 2026-09 machine-loop redesign): PR validation runs arrive as `workflow_dispatch` events fired by the SM (`machine-sm.yml` passes `ci-workflow: ci.yml`), so `github.event_name` is **never** `'pull_request'` on a validation run.

Consequences for this job:

- The `exzone` output is computed only inside the `paths` classifier step, which is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (ci.yml:131) — that step **never executes**. Unlike `core`/`app`/`docs`/`shared`, the output has no `|| steps.filter...` fallback arm either.
- So `needs.changes.outputs.exzone` is empty on **every** event this workflow can fire on (SM validation dispatches, main pushes, tags, schedule, release) → this job always evaluates `'' == 'true'` → **skipped**, every time.
- `quality-gate` is skip-tolerant (`"flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE"` accepts `skipped`), so the aggregate stays green while the JS-engine surface keeps skipping exactly as before. This is the **same green-by-skip bug gh-1280 fixed for `binaries-pr`** ("a broken arch build could never block a merge") and the same latent bug documented for `perf-gate` in the `usage-fold` comment (issue #303).

Net effect: the PR does not deliver AC1 — #1309-class regressions still merge green.

**Fix** — use the idiom this file already established for dispatch-only CI (`binaries-pr`, gh-1280):

```yaml
  flutter-app-exzone:
    ...
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
```

This runs the leg on every SM validation dispatch (where the classifier's non-PR filter arm already treats everything as affected and `build-macos`/`build-ios`/`binaries-pr` macOS legs already run, so the marginal cost is one hosted-macOS leg) and keeps path-narrowing for any future real `pull_request` trigger. # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night). When
  # a PR touches the exclusion zone (flutter_app/lib/apps/**,
  # lib/src/js_ext/**, the guarded family, the guard itself, or the external
  # js_widget_runtime pin in flutter_app/pubspec.yaml), this macos leg runs
  # the family pre-merge, where JavaScriptCore actually loads. Rare paths →
  # one cheap runner; every other PR pays nothing. Nightly keeps the
  # full-suite macOS backstop; merge-blocking flows through the aggregate
  # Quality gate (a red exzone = red gate, AC1's required-and-green).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them

PR validation arrives as `workflow_dispatch` fired by the SM (`machine-sm.yml` passes `ci-workflow: ci.yml`), so `github.event_name` is never `'pull_request'` on a validation run. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1350
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1350
- **Title**: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1267-nightly-premerge-catch` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +98
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T21:34:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T03:04:21Z

## PR Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.
- **Classifier grep** replayed against synthetic positives/negatives AND the real motivating diffs — #1273 (989dfbfff) and gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) both match the path set.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).
- **Review round 1**: bot CHANGES_REQUESTED (dead-code classifier, green-by-skip leg, overstated docs) — all three threads fixed/answered in dc37d9cff.

1. **BLOCKING fixed**: The job `if` is now `(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` — exactly the recommended binaries-pr idiom. 2. **IMPORTANT (dead code) fixed**: The classifier block is now explicitly commented as path-narrowing RESERVE (runs only on a real pull_request event; documented pending in issue #303 like perf/usagefold/intmock). The output declaration has the reserve comment too. ✅

3. **IMPORTANT (docs) fixed**: ci.yml header inventory now says "runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom"; the job comment describes the dispatch model and explicitly drops the "Rare paths → one cheap runner" claim; AGENTS.md now says the leg is path-blind and runs in every SM validation dispatch. ✅

The PR body also updated: mentions "Review round 1: bot CHANGES_REQUESTED ... all three threads fixed/answered in dc37d9cff", and the goal map now says the dispatch-aware classifier is "declined here as separate scope" (natural companion to N4).

Now I need to do a fresh, exhaustive single-pass review of the NEW diff (v2):

1. Verify the rework in the actual repo (checkout should be at the new head dc37d9cff or later).
2. Check the new discussions (26KB now) — round 2 discussions; check the three threads' status and whether the author replied.
3. Look for any NEW issues introduced by the rework:
   - The `if: >-` folded expression — correct YAML folding; operator precedence: `&&` binds tighter than `||` in GitHub expressions — correct.
   - On `workflow_dispatch` with `releaseDispatch: true` input (the gh-1172 real-release dispatch on main) — the exzone leg would fire on that dispatch too! Hmm: `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` — the release dispatch (bare validation dispatches stay inert; releaseDispatch requires refs/heads/main) is also a workflow_dispatch event. So a release dispatch would run the exzone leg (macOS flutter test/apps) — a small cost overlap with the release pipeline. Is that a real problem? Let me think: binaries-pr has the same condition `(pull_request || workflow_dispatch) && (core||shared)` — on a release dispatch, core=true/shared=true (filter arm sets everything true on non-PR events), so binaries-pr also runs the full matrix on release dispatches. So the exzone leg firing on release dispatches is CONSISTENT with the established binaries-pr behavior. The previous round's comment even suggested exactly this idiom. So not a finding — or at most a nit-level observation. The stated design "Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it" — the *schedule* runs are not workflow_dispatch, correct; `release:` published events are not workflow_dispatch, correct; but a manual release dispatch (`releaseDispatch: true` on main) IS workflow_dispatch → leg runs. Minor doc nuance: "Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it" is about event types, and the manual release-dispatch input is an edge. The previous review round itself proposed this exact idiom, so flagging it now as blocking would be hypocritical; as a suggestion it may still be worth noting? # pr-1350: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)

## Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.
- **Classifier grep** replayed against synthetic positives/negatives AND the real motivating diffs — #1273 (989dfbfff) and gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) both match the path set.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

   "body": "🚨 **BLOCKING: `flutter-app-exzone` can never run — the required check stays green-by-skip and the gh-1307 hole this PR targets remains open**

This workflow has **no `pull_request` trigger** (dispatch-only CI, 2026-09 machine-loop redesign): PR validation runs arrive as `workflow_dispatch` events fired by the SM (`machine-sm.yml` passes `ci-workflow: ci.yml`), so `github.event_name` is **never** `'pull_request'` on a validation run.

Consequences for this job:

- The `exzone` output is computed only inside the `paths` classifier step, which is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (ci.yml:131) — that step **never executes**. Unlike `core`/`app`/`docs`/`shared`, the output has no `|| steps.filter...` fallback arm either.
- So `needs.changes.outputs.exzone` is empty on **every** event this workflow can fire on (SM validation dispatches, main pushes, tags, schedule, release) → this job always evaluates `'' == 'true'` → **skipped**, every time.
- `quality-gate` is skip-tolerant (`"flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE"` accepts `skipped`), so the aggregate stays green while the JS-engine surface keeps skipping exactly as before. This is the **same green-by-skip bug gh-1280 fixed for `binaries-pr`** ("a broken arch build could never block a merge") and the same latent bug documented for `perf-gate` in the `usage-fold` comment (issue #303).

Net effect: the PR does not deliver AC1 — #1309-class regressions still merge green.

**Fix** — use the idiom this file already established for dispatch-only CI (`binaries-pr`, gh-1280):

```yaml
  flutter-app-exzone:
    ...
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
```

This runs the leg on every SM validation dispatch (where the classifier's non-PR filter arm already treats everything as affected and `build-macos`/`build-ios`/`binaries-pr` macOS legs already run, so the marginal cost is one hosted-macOS leg) and keeps path-narrowing for any future real `pull_request` trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the nightly `flutter-app-macos` leg remains the backstop there, matching the stated design.

(Alternative: the `usage-fold` form `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'` — but that also fires the macOS leg on every main push, tag, release and 2-hour release-catch-up schedule tick, which is paid coverage nightly already provides.)"

      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)

**Why it can never run.** This workflow has **no `pull_request` trigger** (dispatch-only CI, 2026-09 machine-loop redesign — see the `on:` block: push/workflow_dispatch/release/schedule only). PR validation arrives as `workflow_dispatch` fired by the SM (`machine-sm.yml` passes `ci-workflow: ci.yml`), so `github.event_name` is never `'pull_request'` on a validation run. The `exzone` output is computed only inside the `paths` classifier step, which is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (ci.yml:131) — that step never executes, and unlike `core`/`app`/`docs`/`shared` there is no `steps.filter` fallback arm for `exzone`. So `needs.changes.outputs.exzone` is empty on **every** event this workflow can fire on → `'' == 'true'` → **skipped, every time**.     ...

      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||

```

## PR Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.
- **Classifier grep** replayed against synthetic positives/negatives AND the real motivating diffs — #1273 (989dfbfff) and gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) both match the path set.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).
- **Review round 1**: bot CHANGES_REQUESTED (dead-code classifier, green-by-skip leg, overstated docs) — all three threads fixed/answered in dc37d9cff.

# pr-1350: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)

## Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.
- **Classifier grep** replayed against synthetic positives/negatives AND the real motivating diffs — #1273 (989dfbfff) and gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) both match the path set.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).
- **Review round 1**: bot CHANGES_REQUESTED (dead-code classifier, green-by-skip leg, overstated docs) — all three threads fixed/answered in dc37d9cff.

This workflow has **no `pull_request` trigger** (dispatch-only CI, 2026-09 machine-loop redesign): PR validation runs arrive as `workflow_dispatch` events fired by the SM (`machine-sm.yml` passes `ci-workflow: ci.yml`), so `github.event_name` is **never** `'pull_request'` on a validation run.

Consequences for this job:

- The `exzone` output is computed only inside the `paths` classifier step, which is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (ci.yml:131) — that step **never executes**. Unlike `core`/`app`/`docs`/`shared`, the output has no `|| steps.filter...` fallback arm either.
- So `needs.changes.outputs.exzone` is empty on **every** event this workflow can fire on (SM validation dispatches, main pushes, tags, schedule, release) → this job always evaluates `'' == 'true'` → **skipped**, every time.
- `quality-gate` is skip-tolerant (`"flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE"` accepts `skipped`), so the aggregate stays green while the JS-engine surface keeps skipping exactly as before. This is the **same green-by-skip bug gh-1280 fixed for `binaries-pr`** ("a broken arch build could never block a merge") and the same latent bug documented for `perf-gate` in the `usage-fold` comment (issue #303).

Net effect: the PR does not deliver AC1 — #1309-class regressions still merge green.

**Fix** — use the idiom this file already established for dispatch-only CI (`binaries-pr`, gh-1280):

```yaml
  flutter-app-exzone:
    ...
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
```

This runs the leg on every SM validation dispatch (where the classifier's non-PR filter arm already treats everything as affected and `build-macos`/`build-ios`/`binaries-pr` macOS legs already run, so the marginal cost is one hosted-macOS leg) and keeps path-narrowing for any future real `pull_request` trigger. # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night). When
  # a PR touches the exclusion zone (flutter_app/lib/apps/**,
  # lib/src/js_ext/**, the guarded family, the guard itself, or the external
  # js_widget_runtime pin in flutter_app/pubspec.yaml), this macos leg runs
  # the family pre-merge, where JavaScriptCore actually loads. Rare paths →
  # one cheap runner; every other PR pays nothing. Nightly keeps the
  # full-suite macOS backstop; merge-blocking flows through the aggregate
  # Quality gate (a red exzone = red gate, AC1's required-and-green).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

PR validation arrives as `workflow_dispatch` fired by the SM (`machine-sm.yml` passes `ci-workflow: ci.yml`), so `github.event_name` is never `'pull_request'` on a validation run. ## PR Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.
- **Classifier grep** replayed against synthetic positives/negatives AND the real motivating diffs — #1273 (989dfbfff) and gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) both match the path set.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).
- **Review round 1**: bot CHANGES_REQUESTED (dead-code classifier, green-by-skip leg, overstated docs) — all three threads fixed/answered in dc37d9cff.

# pr-1350: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)

## Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.

- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).

This workflow has **no `pull_request` trigger** (dispatch-only CI, 2026-09 machine-loop redesign): PR validation runs arrive as `workflow_dispatch` events fired by the SM (`machine-sm.yml` passes `ci-workflow: ci.yml`), so `github.event_name` is **never** `'pull_request'` on a validation run.

Consequences for this job:

- The `exzone` output is computed only inside the `paths` classifier step, which is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (ci.yml:131) — that step **never executes**. Unlike `core`/`app`/`docs`/`shared`, the output has no `|| steps.filter...` fallback arm either.
- So `needs.changes.outputs.exzone` is empty on **every** event this workflow can fire on (SM validation dispatches, main pushes, tags, schedule, release) → this job always evaluates `'' == 'true'` → **skipped**, every time.
- `quality-gate` is skip-tolerant (`"flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE"` accepts `skipped`), so the aggregate stays green while the JS-engine surface keeps skipping exactly as before. This is the **same green-by-skip bug gh-1280 fixed for `binaries-pr`** ("a broken arch build could never block a merge") and the same latent bug documented for `perf-gate` in the `usage-fold` comment (issue #303).

Net effect: the PR does not deliver AC1 — #1309-class regressions still merge green.

**Fix** — use the idiom this file already established for dispatch-only CI (`binaries-pr`, gh-1280):

```yaml
  flutter-app-exzone:
    ...
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
```

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night). When
  # a PR touches the exclusion zone (flutter_app/lib/apps/**,
  # lib/src/js_ext/**, the guarded family, the guard itself, or the external
  # js_widget_runtime pin in flutter_app/pubspec.yaml), this macos leg runs
  # the family pre-merge, where JavaScriptCore actually loads. Rare paths →
  # one cheap runner; every other PR pays nothing. Nightly keeps the
  # full-suite macOS backstop; merge-blocking flows through the aggregate
  # Quality gate (a red exzone = red gate, AC1's required-and-green).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2

**Why it can never run.** This workflow has **no `pull_request` trigger** (dispatch-only CI, 2026-09 machine-loop redesign — see the `on:` block: push/workflow_dispatch/release/schedule only). PR validation arrives as `workflow_dispatch` fired by the SM (`machine-sm.yml` passes `ci-workflow: ci.yml`), so `github.event_name` is never `'pull_request'` on a validation run.       (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||

## PR Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.
- **Classifier grep** replayed against synthetic positives/negatives AND the real motivating diffs — #1273 (989dfbfff) and gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) both match the path set.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).

# pr-1350: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)

## Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge:

- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Trigger model — dispatch-only CI (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom, per review)**: ci.yml has **no `pull_request` trigger** — PR validation arrives as an SM `workflow_dispatch` on the head SHA. The leg therefore fires in **every SM validation dispatch** (path-blind; one hosted-macOS leg beside the `build-macos`/`build-ios` legs already paid there), and the `exzone` path set (`flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded family, `native_test_guard.dart`, the `js_widget_runtime` pin in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) is labelled **path-narrowing reserve** — it only narrows if a real `pull_request` trigger ever lands. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip (nightly `flutter-app-macos` stays the full-suite backstop there).
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A red exzone = red gate = no merge.
- Docs de-overstated to the dispatch model: ci.yml header leg inventory, the job's own comment, classifier/output comments, and AGENTS.md §Quality gates (AGENTS.md is agent-injected — the stated invariant must match reality).

**Path-mapping note:** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime); its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin. A lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307); pure CI-config-as-code (no scheduling, no dispatch — SM/owner still own every run, §4b respected); no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) and no bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive): subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment. A dispatch-aware classifier (reviving the pending perf/intmock path-greps, issue #303) is the natural companion slice to N4 — declined here as separate scope.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Trigger truth table** (ruby-YAML structural check): `workflow_dispatch` fires; future `pull_request`+zone fires; future PR-without-zone, `push`, `tag`, `schedule`, `release` all skip. All 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; report + fail-loop wired.

- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. Step-for-step mirrors the nightly macos leg that already passes weekly. No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).
